framingRules._note: What FRAMING a template's media slots want. This is a property of the TEMPLATE, not of the beat — the same entity needs a tight crop for a spatial node and a wide shot for a hero billboard. Declared, not inferred: nothing in the capability measurement says how close a slot crops, so guessing would put full-body shots on marker nodes forever.
framingRules._rule: RANKS, never excludes. A wrong-framing asset sorts last and stays reachable — a crop is an editing decision and 436 of 506 assets carry no framing tag at all. An UNTAGGED asset is never punished; ranking it last would hide most of the library behind a tag nobody has applied.
framingRules._scaleNote: tightest to widest. `quarter` is head-and-chest, TIGHTER than `half`; media_candidates previously mapped it to three_quarter, which is wider than half and the opposite end of the scale.

framingRules._byIdNote: Per-template, from the user watching each clip. `wants: []` is ANY — decided, no preference. A template ABSENT from here is UNDECIDED and ranks every asset equally; the two behave alike today and mean different things, so the distinction is kept in the data.
framingRules._unspecified: A template with no rule wants ANY framing, and every asset ranks on the other signals alone. Silence here means no preference, never 'reject everything'.

notApplicable._why: User 2026-09-23: "the undone 3 are for documents, screenshots and videos." FRAMING IS A PROPERTY OF PERSON MEDIA. A slot holding a screenshot, a document or a piece of footage has no headshot/quarter/half/three_quarter/full — the scale does not describe it. These are DECIDED as not-applicable, not left undecided, and they want a different axis (what KIND of media the slot takes) which does not exist yet.

mediaKindRules._note: What KIND of media a template's slots take. A separate axis from framing: framing answers HOW CLOSE, this answers WHAT IT IS. Three findings arrived at the same gap — the 3 templates where framing does not apply (user 2026-09-23: 'the undone 3 are for documents, screenshots and videos'), the briefs wanting the XXL Freshman cover and album artwork, and brief 23-23's 'screenshots in a document template'.
mediaKindRules._kindNote: person = a photograph of someone. footage = a moving clip. document = an article, screenshot, or anything read as text. artwork = a cover, a sleeve, a poster. graphic = a chart or a generated image. A slot with no rule takes ANY kind.
mediaKindRules._rule: RANKS, never excludes, like framing. An asset whose kind is UNKNOWN sits in the middle, never last — 660 of 1,381 assets carry no kind signal at all and punishing them would hide half the library.
